p.t: In short
**Canva** is the easiest tool for simple images. Photoshop and Illustrator can do more, but take longer to learn.
Keep your Gemini API key secret. Anyone who has it can run jobs on your key and your billing account.
Check your brand colours, fonts and social links before you save the brand file.
Use only images you are allowed to use for your business, and check the licence first.
Use **Canva** (an easy online design tool) for simple graphics. Use **Photoshop** (a full photo editing program) for photos that need fine control.

Shrink images before you upload them, so your store pages load fast.
Build packaging at its exact print size. A 10 x 13 inch mailer is **3000 x 3900 px**.
Keep your **Gemini API key** (a private code that lets the tool use Google's AI) secret. If you see 429 errors, **lower the concurrency** (how many jobs run at once) or add a pause.
For a new logo or banner, hire a designer at **$20 or more**, not a $5 job.
A **free** Canva account (an online design tool) is enough for a basic store's logo, icons and images.
Make logos with a **transparent background** (no background color), so they work on both dark and light sites.

Turn the final logo into a **vector file** (a file that stays sharp at any size).
Check every product cutout **at zoom** (close up) before you publish it.
Shrink images before you upload them. Smaller files make the store load faster.
Free online tools like Canva, Pixlr and Snappa can make simple images, logos and ad pictures.
AI image tools can make pictures from written instructions. Check every picture before you use it.
Put the words "authorized retailer" under a supplier's logo on any badge you make.
Choosing the design tool
**Canva** is the fastest option for simple social posts, product graphics and quick exports.

Canva is an online design app. It has ready-made templates (layouts you fill in), animated icons, graphics, and stock photos and videos (ready-made media you can use). Beginners can build without outside files.
Canva is weak at layering and blending. Layering means stacking objects on top of each other. Blending means mixing one object into another.

Shadows and gradients (smooth colour changes) come in Canva only as presets (fixed options).
You have little control over how one object blends into another.
**Plan designs that do not need deep blending** when you work in Canva.
Canva has no pen tool (a tool that draws exact lines by clicking points) and no real brush.

Canva's draw tool does not auto-correct, so **straight lines** and custom hand-drawn shapes are hard to make.
Build custom shapes in **Illustrator or Photoshop**.
**Photoshop** works mainly with pixels (tiny dots that make up a picture).
Photoshop is built for image manipulation (changing photos).
Examples are cutouts (removing a background), colour grading (adjusting the colour mood) and photo compositing (combining several photos).
Photoshop can also create vector shapes (shapes drawn with maths-based lines that stay sharp at any size). That is why many designers choose it when they can learn only one of the two programs.
**Illustrator** creates scalable vector graphics (graphics that stay sharp when resized), built from mathematical paths (lines defined by maths).

**Enlarging** a logo or shape in Illustrator does not pixelate it (make it blocky).
Illustrator is the right tool for logos, icons and custom drawn shapes.

**Choose the tool by the job**:
**Canva** for speed and ready-made elements.

**Photoshop** for image manipulation and advanced compositing (complex layering of images).
**Illustrator** for custom graphics and shape building.
Choosing the design tool (continued)

One designer can use all three and move files between them.
Photoshop and Illustrator have a **steep learning curve** (they are hard at first).
**Do not try to learn every tool first.** Learn the basic controls, then look up the specific technique you need for the current problem.
Older advice: professional software has unnecessary complexity for basic ecommerce tasks such as resizing and cropping. **Simpler online tools** are more practical for non-designers.
**PicMonkey** is an online editor. It resizes, crops and adds text to images.
PicMonkey needs no software installation or design experience. A free trial is available. The basic plan costs **$7 per month**.
**Snappa** is a simple online tool for custom article images.
Snappa has a free version and a paid version with extra features. It is much simpler than Photoshop and includes a curated set (hand-picked selection) of stock photos.
Canva is **browser-based** (it runs in a web browser, with no install). Its free plan is enough for basic store assets such as logos, favicons (the small icon in a browser tab), banners and icons.
Beginners without design training can use Canva. Experienced designers can use Photoshop or another editor.

Gemini API key setup

Terms:
**Gemini** is Google's AI.

An **API key** is a secret code that lets a tool use your Google AI account.
**Google AI Studio** is Google's website for managing those keys.

Set up the key in Google AI Studio:
1. Open **Get API key**, then **API Keys**.
2. Click **Create API key**.

3. Choose the **Gemini API Key** option.
4. Select an existing project or **create a new one** (a project is a folder that groups your settings).

5. Click **Create key**.
6. Copy the key from the API keys list when a tool needs it.
Treat the Gemini API key **like a password**. Never share it.

Paste the key only into tools you control.
Keep tool files private, because the key is stored inside them.
If a key leaks, **revoke it** (cancel it) in Google AI Studio and create a new one before running anything else.
Downloading course HTML tool files from Google Drive (Google's online file storage): **click the three-dot menu** on each file and choose Download. HTML files are web pages that run in a browser.

Do not open the raw code.
**Download every file of the set** before first use, then open the HTML file locally in a browser.
Gemini image generation (Nano Banana, the nickname of Google's image model) runs in the browser tools on the model **gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview**.
Model names change. If a request returns a 404 error (a "not found" message), check the Gemini API models documentation and **update the model field** in the tool.
Adding the key through a skill file (source procedure). A skill file is a folder of instructions that Claude can load:
1. In Claude, open **Settings > Customize skills**, click **Add**, and add the image skill folder.

2. Open https://aistudio.google.com/apikey and sign in with a Google account.
3. Click **Create API key**.

4. Copy the key, which starts with AIza.
5. Open the SKILL.md file and find the API Config section.
6. Replace the placeholder line API KEY = 'YOUR GEMINI API KEY HERE' with your key, then **save the file**.
Gemini API key setup (continued)
**Conflict:** the skill-file procedure above places the key inside a file. A key placed in a skill file travels with that file.
Anyone you share the skill with can run jobs on your key and your billing account (the account that gets charged).

Use the file method **only for a private skill** that is never shared or uploaded.
Otherwise, **enter the key in the tool's key field** at run time.
Never place the key inside a file you share or upload.

p.t:
A **palette** is a set of colours that already work together.
**Color Hunt** (colorhunt.co) shows pre-made palettes.
Search by colour name or browse trending palettes.
Hover over a palette to see all its **hex codes**, ready for design tools and websites.
Canva's free page at canva.com/learn/100-color-combinations offers curated palettes with hex codes, mood associations (feelings each colour gives) and design examples.
This page is useful when you are **unsure of your brand colours**. Older advice.

Canva palettes are arranged around the **hue** at the top. The hue is the main colour type, such as red or blue.
**Tint** moves the hue toward white.

**Tone** moves it toward grey.
**Shade** moves it toward black.
Use these controls to **soften a colour** instead of choosing a random new one.
A browser colour-picker extension (a small add-on for your browser) reads the exact button colour from a store's website.

So a pop-up button can **match it**.
The **Eyedropper** in the Canva colour palette picks any colour from an image.

In Photoshop, press **X** to swap the foreground and background colours.
Press **D** to reset them to black and white.
Brushes, masks (tools that hide parts of an image) and gradients use these colours. Resetting avoids painting in the wrong colour.
Canva Brand Kit
Term: the **Brand Kit** is Canva's place to save your logo, colours and fonts.

The Brand Kit is available on the free plan and allows **three brand colours**.
Path: **Brand Kit > Brand colours > add colours**.

Black and white can be used alongside them.
Saved colours then appear under the text colour option, so you **do not need to remember exact codes**.
The Brand Kit lets you upload a logo, a colour scheme and fonts, then apply them to any design with **one click**.
When a brand colour is missing, Canva can pull colours from an uploaded image.
**Google Fonts** (fonts.google.com) offers free fonts licensed for commercial use (for business).
Search by name, or filter by style such as **serif** (letters with small strokes at the ends), **sans-serif** (clean letters without them) or **display** (large decorative fonts).
**Download** them and upload them to design tools or Shopify themes (website templates for Shopify, an online shop platform) without licence risk.
Canva's Text panel lets you search fonts by style, such as handwriting, corporate, display, serif, sans serif, luxury, elegant or vintage.

The Text panel includes most popular Google Fonts.
The presenter's favourites were **Lato, Montserrat, Open Sans and Rubik**.

Use **Open Sans** as a plain sans-serif font for readable ad copy.
If you have a brand font, **swap it in** instead.

Keep body copy (the main text paragraphs) in a clean sans-serif, not decorative fonts.
This keeps text **easy to read** on small screens.
Use the **brand serif font** for packaging text, so the packaging matches the brand's typography (its letter style).
Kittl brand guidelines

Term: **brand guidelines** is a document that sets out your brand's rules.
Kittl (an online design tool) has **free** brand guidelines templates.

Workflow: **Templates > search "brand guidelines" > choose a free template > open it**.
In the left sidebar, open the **Project Colors** panel.

Click a colour, then **replace its hex code** with your new one and press Enter.
All instances of that colour **update automatically**.
Hold **Option** (Mac) or **Alt** (Windows) and drag an element to duplicate it.
This is faster than copy-paste when you create multiple texture variations in brand guidelines.

Brand guidelines templates **do not support batch font replacement** (changing all fonts at once) across the document.
**Update each text instance** one by one.

Plan for manual font updates.
The Brand Guidelines template shows project colours in code format.

The screenshot in the source shows the values **540863 and 24984o**. Check them before use.
The **Browse Color Palettes** option gives more palettes.
Terms:

**MCP** (Model Context Protocol) is a standard way to connect an AI like Claude to outside services.
**JSON** is a plain text format for data.

**ICP** means ideal customer profile, your perfect buyer.
**Brand Fetch MCP** is a data extraction tool (a tool that pulls data from websites). It has two main functions.
**get_brand** returns the visual identity as JSON: logos, colours, fonts, social handles (account names) and company metadata (basic company facts).
**get_brand_context** returns the voice (how the brand talks), ICP, positioning (where the brand stands against others), product catalogue, tagline, mission and target audiences.
Brandfetch MCP is a Model Context Protocol connector for Claude.

It extracts brand identity from any website: logo, hex colour codes, fonts, social media links and brand summary.
It generates two files, **brandkit.json** and **voice.md**.

Processing takes **5 to 7 minutes** before the brand kit and voice files are returned.
**Naming difference:** names the two functions **get_brand** and get_brand_context.
lists six tools: Search Brands, Build Logo URLs, Identify Merchant from Transaction, Fetch Asset as Base64, Get Brand Details and Get Brand Context.
Brandfetch MCP (brand data extraction) (continued)
Base64 is a way of writing a file as text. A merchant is the shop that received a payment.
The **read-only tools** (tools that only read data and change nothing) extract logos, hex colours, fonts, social links and merchant data when you run the brand kit prompt.

**Competitor research:** use Brand Fetch MCP to study competitor brands' positioning, colours and voice.
**Do not copy** their visual identity or tone.

Use it as **competitive intelligence** (information about rivals) to understand market positioning.
Install in Claude (setting):

**Customize > Connectors > click the plus button** > enter the name Brandfetch MCP > paste the MCP server URL from developers.brandfetch.com/dashboard into the Remote MCP server URL field > **click Add** >

click Connect and authorise.
Full setup procedure:
1. Go to brandfetch.com.
2. Click **Join Brandfetch**.

3. Click **Are you a developer? Get API keys** (not Get started).
4. Sign up via Google, GitHub or email to access developers.brandfetch.com/dashboard.

5. Go to **Plans & Billing** and confirm the free tier ($0 per month, 100 requests).
6. Go to **Keys & MCP** and copy the Brandfetch MCP URL.

7. Open your Claude Cowork Project.
8. Go to **Customize > Connectors**.
9. Click the **plus button** (Add custom connector).

10. Enter **Brandfetch MCP** as the name.
11. Paste the MCP URL into **Remote MCP server URL**.
12. Click **Add**.

13. Click **Connect** and complete authorisation.
Verification after pulling data:
If Brandfetch returns incomplete data, or cannot detect a field such as the heading font, offer to have Claude **visit the live website** to verify and retrieve the missing information.

This is faster than asking you for details you may not recall.
Verify in this order **before saving the final brandkit.json file**, and fix any discrepancies (differences):
1. **Primary brand colour:** show the hex code and ask the user to confirm it matches the colour on their main buttons.
2. **Heading or title font:** if Brandfetch detected it, confirm it with the user. If not, request it directly or retrieve it from the live site.
3. **Social media links:** confirm each one (Instagram, Facebook, etc.) is current and correct.
Logos

Canva is a simple option for creating a logo yourself when the design is basic.
Canva's free plan is enough for logos, favicons and icons.
**Fiverr** (an online marketplace where freelance designers sell their work) is the recommended platform for logo design at startup.
Fiverr balances affordability with quality.

Fiverr offers a curated marketplace where you can browse portfolios (a designer's sample work), compare prices and read reviews before buying.
Older advice.
Filter Fiverr's logo section by your **maximum budget** (set to 100 USD in the source), desired style and delivery time.
This narrows the 183,000+ available services to your needs.

When evaluating Fiverr designers, prioritise those with **1,000+ completed jobs** and 4.8+ star ratings.
Designers with 50+ solid reviews are also dependable.
Many Fiverr logo designers specialise in one aesthetic (style): minimalist, mascot, hand-drawn or vintage.
With a specific style preference, search for designers who **specialise in that style** rather than generalists (designers who do everything).
**Request a source file** in Photoshop or Adobe Illustrator format from the designer.

A source file is the editable original. With it, the logo can be edited later **without starting from scratch**.
Fiverr logo procedure:

1. **Choose three hex colour codes** (primary, accent, button) and record them.
2. On Fiverr.com, navigate to **Graphics & Design > Logo Design**.
3. **Filter by budget** (under 100 USD) and review designer portfolios, ratings and reviews.
4. Click on a designer whose style you like and review their package details and revision policy.
5. Click **Continue** to proceed to checkout and provide your business name, colour codes, business description and target market feel.

6. Complete payment via credit card or PayPal.
7. Receive your logo files in the specified timeframe.

8. **Request revisions** if needed, then download and accept the final files.
Building logos by hand:
Illustrator's **Shape Builder** merges overlapping shapes into one outline when you drag across them.
Logos (continued)

Hold **Alt or Option** while dragging to remove unwanted areas.
It is the main method for building logos from several overlapping shapes.

**Use separate shapes** for each part of a logo or icon.
Then combine them with the Shape Builder, rather than drawing the final outline in one go.
This makes it easier to correct one part without redrawing the whole mark.
**Canva logo export:** when downloading a logo, choose **JPG** (a common image file type) as the file type.

Raise the quality slider from the default **80 percent to 100 percent**.
The default export size shown was 500 by 500 pixels.

For a logo on coloured backgrounds, a **transparent PNG** is the cleanest option.
Make one by using a free online background remover (search for background image remover).
The tool **deletes a white background**, so the PNG becomes transparent.
Use **royalty-free** image sources for product photos. Royalty-free means you do not pay a fee for each use.

Examples are Google's royalty-free image search or the free stock site Pixabay.
These are **safer than competitor photos**.
Older advice.
Google Image Search with the filter **Labeled for commercial reuse** (Settings > Usage rights > Labeled for commercial reuse) gives free, legally usable product images.

Use these for demo stores (test shops with sample products) **without buying licences**.
Older advice (2020).
Stock photo route: start with Google Image Search.

Then refine with free royalty-free stock sites (20+ options listed in the source).
You need **at most 10 images** for 5 demo products plus a homepage banner.

Use **Canva** for product images.
Use Google royalty-free image search for product images **without people** when Canva has none.
Older advice (2021).

**Unsplash** offers free stock photos.
For a discount pop-up (a small box on the shop page), search a keyword such as **gift**.

For a chat avatar (the small profile picture in chat), search **man or woman**.
Download the image and upload it into the app.

**123RF** has millions of images at $2 to $3 per photo.
Use it when supplier images (photos from your product supplier) are unavailable or low quality.

Older figure (2021).
**Snappa** includes a curated set (hand-picked selection) of stock photos.
Canva's built-in stock photos are **paid only on the paid plan** (see plans table).
Product images: AI generation
Term: an **AI image generator** creates pictures from a text instruction called a **prompt**.

**Gemini (NanoBanana)** is the recommended AI image generator for demo product images.
Any AI image generator can be used.

Visit **gemini.google.com** for Google's free AI image generation service.
Copy the complete Source A Image Prompt.

Replace the placeholder product name (a fill-in word) with your product name.
This section shows only the **first line** of the prompt. Take the full text from the source course.
You are a professional e-commerce product photographer creating images for a premium Shopify store
Replace "product name goes here" in the full prompt with **your chosen product name**.
Gemini image generation **costs little per image**, which makes large batches (many images at once) affordable.
For photorealistic UGC-style scenes (realistic images that look like customer photos; UGC means user-generated content), some 2026 testers rated ChatGPT's image model as more realistic.

**Run the same scene prompt through both** on a small test set before choosing one for a full batch.
**ChatGPT** (version 5.2 as shown in the source) is used for:

packaging mockups from inspiration images and brand references.
Canva Magic Media (Canva's AI image tool):

Canva Magic Media gives **50 free unique images** on the free account.
It gives **500 per month** on the paid account.
Canva Text to Image generates unique images from a text description.
The images can serve as stock images for demo products **without copyright issues** (legal ownership problems).

This applies **as long as the image is not for sale** to anyone else.
Creating AI product images in Canva:

1. Open Canva and **create a new project**.
2. Click **Apps** in the sidebar and search for **Magic Media**.

3. Type a descriptive prompt (example: blue surfboard on white background).
4. Click **Create your image** and wait for generation.

5. Drag the result onto your canvas.
6. Click **Share > Download as PNG**.
Background removal and cut-outs
Terms: a **cut-out** is a product separated from its background. **Background removal** deletes the background.

Canva background removal (Edit photo):
Select the product photo and open **Edit photo**.

Use the background removal option to **cut out the product automatically**.
The result is **not always perfect**.

Use the adjust options to add back or erase parts of the cutout.
Select **Remove background**, then use **Adjust** for small areas.
Edit photo includes a **Background remover** that removes the background of an uploaded product image automatically.

A brush tool then removes leftover parts.
**Auto-focus** blurs the background around a subject.
The **Shadow** option adds a shadow to an element.

PhotoRoom (AI product scenes):
PhotoRoom is an AI app for product photos.
It cuts out an object, such as a coffee cup, and places it on **instant backgrounds** such as wood countertops, bathrooms and jungles.

It creates reflections and shadows.
It is available on mobile and desktop.
Product photos in PhotoRoom:

1. Choose **Start from photo**, then **Camera**.
2. **Cut out** the product.
3. Choose **Instant backgrounds** and pick a background from the list. The app fills in several backgrounds.

4. Adjust the image with the **shadows and highlights** controls and with **background blur**.
A phone snapshot can be **pixelated** (blocky).

A low-resolution source (a small, low-detail picture) gives a poor result.
**Use a better source photo**.
In PhotoRoom's desktop editor, a **Shadows drop-down** (a menu that opens from a button) adjusts shadows and highlights across the whole image.

The background options include a **blur switch** that softens the backdrop behind the cut-out.
The blur makes the product **stand out**.

Photoshop and other cut-out options:
**Clipping Magic** (about $5 per month) removes image backgrounds.
It produces cut-out product PNGs for floating images (product images shown with no background).
**Unscreen** (video background removal) and similar tools can extend a background image.
Background removal and cut-outs (continued)
A **generative fill** tool (AI that adds new image content) expands a cropped hero background (the large banner image at the top of a page).

Photoshop's **Select Subject** command detects the main subject automatically.
The **Object Selection** tool and **Lasso** tool add or remove areas.

Use them together when the automatic result misses parts of the subject.
Cut out a subject with **Select and Mask**:

1. Open the **Select** menu and choose **Subject**, or use the Select Subject button in the toolbar.
2. Click **Select and Mask** to open the refinement panel.
3. Use the brush to add missing parts, and hold **Alt or Option** to subtract unwanted areas.
4. In the edge settings, use **Smooth** to soften jagged edges, **Feather** for a soft edge, and **Contrast** to sharpen the edge.
5. Drag **Shift Edge** inward slightly to remove white fringing (a thin light line) around the outline.

6. Click **Output To** and choose **Layer Mask** so the cutout stays editable.
Photoshop masks hide or reveal areas of a layer.
**White reveals, black hides**.

The invert shortcut is **Ctrl+I or Cmd+I**.
Masks cut an object out **without deleting pixels**, so the edit can be undone at any time.
Painting with the eraser on a normal image layer is **destructive**: removed pixels cannot be restored.
**Apply the removal to a layer mask** so the original image stays intact.
Product image editing and backgrounds
To set a photo as a background, drag it onto the page, right-click it (or two-finger click on a trackpad) and choose **Set image as background**.

Then move the image so the important part is visible.
Canva's **undo** reverts the last change. This lets you try fonts, colours and sizes without losing your work.
Canva templates are ready-made layouts you can search by keyword, for example blog. Use **Use Template** or **Add as new page**. Templates speed up designs such as blog headers and sale banners.
Canva Source A templates: open the provided link. It opens a template already sized for the Manhattan theme. Then click **Use Template** to start editing.
A free online background remover deletes a white background, so the PNG becomes transparent. A PNG is a picture file format that can have see-through areas.
A transparent PNG is the cleanest option for logos and icons on coloured backgrounds.
Photoshop
**Generative Fill** can add or change parts of an image using AI. It can be used alongside AI background tools.
Generative Fill creates or replaces content from a selected area and a text prompt (the written instruction you type). At the time of writing it was at an early stage with uneven results.

**Expect several tries** before you accept one.
Adding realistic light falloff (the gradual darkening of light across a surface) to a cut-out subject:
1. Create an **Exposure** adjustment layer above the subject. An adjustment layer changes how the image looks without changing its pixels (the tiny dots that make up the picture).

Lower the exposure so the subject matches the darker background.
2. **Clip** the exposure layer to the subject, so it affects only that subject.
3. Press **Cmd+I** or **Ctrl+I** to invert its mask. A mask is a black-and-white layer that shows or hides an effect. Inverting fills the mask black, which hides the effect.
4. Set a soft brush with low opacity (how see-through the paint is). Paint **white** over the areas that should be darker, such as parts not lit by the background light.
5. Add a solid colour or **Hue/Saturation** layer clipped to the subject, to match the colour of the background light.
6. Set the layer to a blending mode (a rule for how two layers mix) such as **Overlay** or **Color Burn**. Then use the **Blend If** sliders to blend the colour into the subject.
Hold **Alt or Option** to split the sliders for a smoother blend.

**Blend If** sliders (in Blending Options) blend a layer based on the brightness of the layer below. Holding **Alt or Option** while dragging splits the slider for a smooth transition instead of a hard edge.
**Clipping mask**: hold **Alt or Option** and click the line between two layers. This applies an adjustment layer only to the layer beneath it.
Without clipping, an adjustment layer affects the whole artboard (the working area of the design).
Adjustment layers change colour, brightness, contrast, levels, curves, exposure, hue and saturation, photo filters and colour balance. They do not change the underlying pixels.
Each adjustment can be turned off or edited later, so it counts as a **non-destructive** edit (one you can undo at any time).
Scaling a **rasterised** pixel image (one made of fixed dots) makes it pixelated (blocky). A **smart object** (a protected container that keeps the original quality) keeps its quality when resized.
**Convert the layer to a smart object before scaling**. A smart object cannot be painted on directly.
Right-click a layer and choose **Convert to Smart Object**. To edit its contents, click the smart object icon at the bottom right of the layer thumbnail. Change the content and save.
The change updates everywhere the smart object is used.
Resizing and compressing for the store
Canva free has no resize tool.
For a different banner size, go to **Canva Home > Create a design > Custom size**, enter the dimensions, and recreate the banner.
Canva paid resizes existing designs with its built-in **resize tool**.
**Bulk Resize** is a browser tool with no sign-up and batch processing (many files at once). It resizes and compresses image files and converts them to PNG or JPEG (a common photo format).
It can reduce size from about **2.3 MB to about 54 KB**.
Hero background image (the large picture at the top of a page): resize to about **1,200 px wide** as JPEG with reduced quality (about 40 to 50 KB) for faster load speed.

Set the main page size to about 700 px on desktop.
**Compress** image files before uploading, to reduce the impact on page load. **ImageOptim** is a free desktop app for Mac.
Windows has built-in image compression. Setup and usage instructions are in Microsoft's official support documentation.

Canva technique reference (continued)
Canva technique reference
Hold **Shift** while clicking elements to select several at once. Or drag a box across them to select everything inside it, then move them as a group.
Pressing Shift again on a selected object removes it from the selection.
Drag a **corner handle** with Shift held to keep the aspect ratio locked while resizing. Corner handles resize both directions. Side handles resize one direction.
After the ratio is set, release Shift and drag a handle to reshape.
Hold **Alt on Windows or Option on Mac** while dragging an element or handle to work from its centre point instead of an edge. The same key **duplicates** an element when dragged.
This is faster than copy and paste for repeated items.
Hold **Shift while dragging** to lock movement to one direction. The element will not move up or down while you move it left or right. Zoom with **Ctrl (Windows) or Cmd (Mac)** while scrolling.

**Pink snap lines** appear while dragging an element. They help you align it to the left, centre or right edge of another element.
Align and space objects:

1. Hold **Shift** and click the objects you want to align, or drag a box around them.
2. Open the **Position** menu in the top toolbar.

3. Choose the alignment you need: left, centre, right, top, middle or bottom.
4. Choose **Space evenly** horizontally or vertically to make the gaps equal.
5. If the spacing still looks uneven, **group the objects first**, then apply Space evenly.
Press **Ctrl+G (Windows) or Cmd+G (Mac)** to group selected objects, so they move as one unit. Double-click an object inside a group to isolate it. Ungroup with **Ctrl+Shift+G or Cmd+Shift+G**.
Right-click an element, open **Layer**, and choose **Bring Forward** or **Send Backward**. **Ctrl+[ or Cmd+[** moves an element one layer back.
**Ctrl+] or Cmd+]** moves it one layer forward. Adding **Alt** sends it to the very back or very front.
Every element sits on its own layer, and stacking order decides what is on top. Text placed first sits under shapes placed later. **Move layers on purpose** when a design looks wrong.
Effects and editing
Shadows and gradients: search **Elements** for "shadow gradient" or "shadow. This gives many ready-made options in dark and light, long and short versions.
Place them behind text or a product to add depth.
Speech bubbles: Canva has fewer layout and text-bubble options than Photoshop, so speech-bubble testimonials are harder to build in it.
Plan the layout around that limit, build the bubble parts elsewhere, or keep the Canva version to **plain quote cards**.
Canva **Edit photo**'s **Shadow** option adds a shadow to an element.
Photoshop technique reference
**Free Transform**: **Ctrl+T (Windows) or Cmd+T (Mac)**. Hold Shift to lock the ratio while scaling.
Right-click the transform to choose **Warp**, which bends or distorts the shape.
Press **V** to return to the Selection tool. Hold **Alt or Option** while dragging to duplicate an object. Hold **Shift** while drawing a shape to keep it square or circular.
Alt or Option while dragging a shape from its centre draws it outward from the centre point.
To make a shape blurred, such as a soft shadow, **rasterise or convert it to a smart object**. Then choose **Filter > Blur > Gaussian Blur** (a smooth, even blur).
Lower the **Fill opacity** in the layer panel to make the shadow subtler.
Double-click a layer to open **Blending Options** (Layer Properties). **Darken** removes whites from the layer above. **Lighten** removes darks.
**Overlay** merges the two layers.
**Drop shadow**: add it from the **FX panel** at the bottom of the Layers panel. Settings include angle, opacity, distance, spread and size. These control direction, strength and softness.
Repair
**Spot Healing Brush** removes blemishes (marks), dust and small unwanted objects with one click or brush stroke.
**Clone Stamp** copies pixels from a sampled area. Hold **Alt or Option**, click the source, then paint over the spot.
Press **V** for the **Selection tool**, which moves whole objects.

Press **A** for the **Direct Selection tool**, which moves single anchor points (the dots on a line) or line segments. Use the **Pen tool** with the anchor point tools to add, remove or convert points on a path (a line or shape outline).

**Brush tool**: Tool Options has a slider between **Accuracy and Smoothness**. Move it toward Smoothness for smoother, less exact strokes. Move it toward Accuracy for strokes that follow the mouse path closely.
**Clipping mask**: place a shape and an image together, then press **Ctrl+7 (Windows) or Cmd+7 (Mac)**. This hides everything outside the shape.
Double-click the masked image to move or resize the image inside the shape.
**Polygon tool** creates shapes with a chosen number of sides. Press the **Up or Down arrow key** while dragging to add or remove sides.
**Text tool**: drag to create a text box of a set size. Then type, or use **Lorem Ipsum** (dummy placeholder text) for mockups. Use the **Properties panel** to set size, line spacing and alignment.
Illustrator, Photoshop and Premiere Pro (a video editing program) work together.
A file placed in one Adobe app can be opened in its original program, edited and saved. The change then updates in the other app.
This makes it practical to build a graphic in Illustrator and use it in a video edit.
Animation in Photoshop and Illustrator requires a separate program, **After Effects**. Canva offers simple built-in animations instead, such as rise, pan, fade and pop effects.
Practical workflow: start with **Canva** for speed. Switch to **Photoshop** for photos and composites (images built from several parts) that need control. Use **Illustrator** for custom graphics.
Keep originals editable with masks, adjustment layers and smart objects, so changes can be made later.

A **vector file** (a file made of math lines, not pixels) scales to any size without losing quality.

**Command+Shift+

A cutout is the product cut away from its background.
Quick background removal in Canva:

2. **Choose Remove background** and let Canva process it.
3. **Check the result.** If the cutout is good, it is ready to use.
4. If the cutout misses parts or leaves specks, **open Adjust, then Configure.**
5. **Use Remove** to cut out more of the background, or **Restore** to bring back parts removed by mistake.

6. **Change the brush size** in the Configure menu and zoom into problem areas for finer work.
7. **Use the Erase tool** to delete small leftover bits, lumps or blemishes.

8. Optionally **set a light grey background color** that matches the website's color scheme.
The quick method is fast but limited.

It **cannot reliably remove blemishes** on products or clothing.
Shadows are harder to handle than in **Photoshop** (Adobe's pixel-editing program).

Use it **when speed matters more than perfect edges**.
Canva's quick removal trades quality for speed.
For high-end product photography with clean edges and no visible black lines, **the Photoshop workflow gives better results**.

Then **refine the edges manually**. The brush handles small gaps.

Photoshop: brush and retouching
**Brush size and feather shortcut**: hold **Alt**, hold right-click, and move left or right to change brush size.

Move up or down to change **feather** (how soft the brush edge is).
**Alt plus mouse wheel** zooms in and out.

**Spot Healing Brush** removes small spots, hairs and blemishes by blending them with the surrounding area.
**Feather it slightly** so the fix blends in.

**Work with short, sharp clicks** instead of dragging, since dragging smooths the area out.
Use the Spot Healing Brush with the same **Alt plus right-click drag** as the brush.
**Keep the brush small** and use a little feather so the repaired spot blends with its surroundings.
Using Spot Healing with a large brush or on high-contrast edges **changes the texture around it too much**.

**Keep the brush small** and check each click in areas with strong contrast.
**Clone Stamp** copies pixels from one area to another.

**Hold Alt** to set the source point, release Alt, then paint over the target area.
The copied area keeps its lighting. It can look too bright or too dark when moved.

**Watch the light direction.**
The Clone Stamp source moves with the cursor. So a long stroke copies the sampled spot repeatedly and creates visible duplicates.

**Sample a new source area with Alt-click** often.
Avoid dragging across the same sampled spot for a long distance.
Sample from different points. Drag the source from the side where the light falls on the same surface.
**Adjustment layers** (the circle icon at the bottom of the Layers panel) apply changes above the photo.

These changes include exposure, hue/saturation, black and white, or whites and blacks.
They do this **without altering the photo's pixels**.

**Dragging the adjustment layer to the trash** removes the change and restores the original image.
In **Hue/Saturation**, hue sets the color itself.

Saturation sets how strong that color is.
To reduce a color cast (an unwanted tint) on a garment against a white background, **lower saturation**.

Lowering saturation moves the color toward grey or black **instead of changing the hue**.
Lowering Saturation on a tinted area, such as a blue cast on a white T-shirt, **neutralizes it**.
Used as an adjustment layer, **the original photo stays unchanged**.

ImageOptim is a desktop app for Mac. A desktop app is a program you install on your computer. ImageOptim **compresses** images, which means it makes the file smaller. Drag the image into its window.
